title: Cross-Domain Access, Change, Vendor & Travel Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines a unified set of policies and end-to-end procedures for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and travel. The goal is to reduce approval friction, eliminate duplicate reviews, and ensure auditable, compliant decisions for cross-functional requests that span multiple teams.

Scope:
- Applies to any request or activity that touches two or more of the following domains: Access, Change, Data, Procurement/Expenses, Vendor Relationships, Travel.
- Examples: onboarding a contractor that requires VPN & host access + expense reimbursement; purchasing a third-party SaaS that ingests customer data; global travel for vendor onboarding that requires travel advance.
- Out of scope: purely team-local tasks that do not touch shared infrastructure, billing, or customer data.

Principles:
1. Least privilege: grant the minimum access required and review periodically.
2. Single source of truth: approvals are recorded in the company procurement/approval system and linked to ticket IDs.
3. Separation of duties: procurement/finance approvals are separate from technical access approvals.
4. Time-boxed elevated access: any break-glass or temporary privilege must have an explicit owner, expiry, and audit trail.
5. Risk-based exceptions: higher risk requests require additional controls (encryption, contract clauses, SOC2 evidence).

Roles and ownership:
- Requester: initiates the ticket and provides justification, risk assessment, and business owner.
- Business Owner: owns the business need, defines required data access level, and accepts residual risk.
- Technical Approver: IAM or systems owner granting access or approving change.
- Finance/Procurement Approver: approves spend or contract terms.
- Security Reviewer: required for any request involving customer data, vendor-hosted compute, or cross-border data flow.
- Approvals Coordinator (Ops): ensures sequencing and records final audit link.

Approval matrix (summary):
- Low risk (internal tooling, no customer data, <$2k): Team lead approval.
- Medium risk (non-production infra, limited customer data exposure, $2k–$50k): Technical Approver + Finance.
- High risk (production access, customer data, >$50k): Technical Approver + Finance + Security + Legal.

Procedures (step-by-step):
1) Create request in the approval system (use template: Request Type, Rationale, Business Owner, Affected Systems, Estimated Cost, Data Sensitivity Level).
2) Auto-routing: system routes to Technical Approver & Finance in parallel. Security is CC'd if Data Sensitivity >= PII or vendor-hosted.
3) Temporary access: if needed immediately, requester can request a 24–72 hour ephemeral token (requires justification and post-mortem).
4) Procurement: Finance issues PO or card provisioning after approvals. All vendor contracts > $10k go to Legal for review.
5) Implementation: Technical Approver implements change during approved maintenance windows unless emergency.
6) Post-implementation: requester completes the verification checklist and closes the ticket. Approvals Coordinator publishes audit link to the ticket.

Change Management specifics:
- All changes that touch production or customer data require a Change Request (CR) with: rollback plan, impact matrix, test plan, and SLO rollback criteria.
- Maintenance window policy: standard windows (Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC) unless otherwise agreed. Emergency changes must use the incident change path and include a post-change review within 72 hours.
- Change SLO: 95% of non-emergency CRs should be processed within 5 business days from submission to scheduled window.

Access & Permissions rules:
- Onboarding: access requests must map to predefined roles in IAM. If a custom role is needed, Technical Approver must document permissions and justify deviation.
- Reviews: recurring access certification every 90 days for sensitive roles (production admin, DB access, key management).
- Break-glass: issued by Engineering SRE leads with a max duration of 48 hours and mandatory audit logging.

Data management and vendor data handling:
- Data classification: PUBLIC | INTERNAL | CONFIDENTIAL | RESTRICTED. Vendor data handling requirements are tied to classification.
- Data transfer: cross-border transfers require Legal sign-off for vendors that will host or process RESTRICTED data.
- Vendor onboarding checklist includes: SOC2/ISO evidence, encryption at transit and rest, retention policy alignment, subprocessors list, and a data breach notification SLA (max 72 hours).

Procurement & expenses:
- Spend thresholds: 
  - <$2k: local card or petty cash with team lead attestation.
  - $2k–$50k: Finance approval required and PO issued.
  - >$50k: Finance + Legal + Executive sponsor.
- Travel advance: up to 50% of estimated trip cost can be requested; all advances require a trip purpose, vendor contact, and pre-approved budget code.
- Expense policy: expenses must be submitted within 30 days of completion; exceptions require manager sign-off.

Vendor management and contracting:
- Risk tiers: Tier 1 (critical infra/customer data), Tier 2 (business-critical but no customer data), Tier 3 (low-risk SaaS).
- Tier 1 vendors require dedicated SLAs, redundancy planning, quarterly security reviews, and an executive sponsor.
- Contract playbook: define termination rights, data return/destruction, audit rights, and breach notification timelines.

Travel policies (cross-border & vendor onboarding travel):
- Pre-travel: travelers must submit a trip request with security checklist if visiting vendor premises. The travel request auto-triggers a vendor risk brief when visiting Tier 1 vendors.
- Insurance: company travel insurance covers overseas vendor onboarding trips; travelers must enroll at least 7 days prior.
- Expenses: per-diem policy by country; exceptions need pre-approval.

Sequencing & concurrent approvals (how to avoid blocking):
- Use parallel approval routing where possible: Finance and Technical Approver operate in parallel; security review can be conditional (only for medium/high-risk).
- Approvals Coordinator responsibilities: ensure sequence for actions that must occur in order (e.g., sign contract before issuing credentials).

Templates and examples (copy into approval system):
- Procurement request (JSON example):
{ "request_type": "SaaS Vendor Purchase", "business_owner": "<name>", "estimated_cost": "$12,500", "data_classification": "INTERNAL", "vendor_tier": "Tier 2" }

- Access request CLI snippet (example):
$ rwdctl access request --user alice --role db-reader --reason "support migration" --expires 2026-04-01

Audit and metrics to monitor:
- Weekly: number of cross-domain requests, average approval time per domain, percent of requests routed to Security.
- Monthly: number of temporary access grants, number of post-change incidents, vendor risk posture changes.
- KPIs: 90% of low-risk requests processed within 48 hours; reduction in duplicate approvals by 50% in the first 6 months after adoption.

Exception handling & escalation:
1) Risk exception request: documented in the approval system, signed by Business Owner + Security + Legal for high-risk exceptions.
2) Emergency escalation: use the incident hotline and mark the ticket as emergency change; post-facto approvals must be attached within 72 hours.

Operational runbook pointers (quick links):
- Request creation guide: /confluence/policies-and-process/procurement-requests
- IAM role catalog: /confluence/eng-infra/iam-roles
- Vendor onboarding checklist: /confluence/policies-and-process/vendor-onboarding-checklist

Appendix: sample approval matrix (text table)
| Request type | Data sensitivity | Cost band | Approvers | SLA |
| SaaS (no data) | INTERNAL | <$2k | Team Lead | 48h |
| SaaS (vendor processes data) | CONFIDENTIAL | $2k–$50k | Tech + Finance (+ Security if CONFIDENTIAL) | 5bd |
| Infra change (prod) | RESTRICTED | any | Tech + Security + Finance + Exec | 7bd |

- 2026-03-01: updated clarifications for travel advance and vendor SLAs; added procurement JSON template.

End of document.
